Caption: Two systems, one truth - and they never agree on the first pass.
The gap isn't error. It's timing, mapping and manual edits stacked up.
Source A is the ledger. Source B is the ops feed. Neither one is wrong.

A roll-forward is the running bridge from last month's closed balance to this month's, adding every posted movement in order so the ending figure you show your manager can be traced line by line back to a number they already signed off, and nothing appears on it that you cannot point at and name.
Start the reconciliation from the balance you already agreed. Never from zero.
Post each movement once, in date order. One line, one cause.

A reconciling item is any single difference between the two sources that you can name, date and assign a cause to; if you cannot yet say what it is and why it is there it is not a reconciling item, it is an unexplained variance, and an unexplained variance is the one thing you never carry forward into next month.
If the bridge doesn't tie to the penny, you're not done - you're guessing.
Set the line where a difference stops being worth your evening.

A materiality threshold is the dollar figure below which a reconciling difference is logged but not investigated, chosen so the hours you spend chasing a variance never cost more than the variance itself; most working managers set it far too low and lose their evenings to rounding that never mattered.
Walk one real exception all the way to its cause before you generalise.
This is the customer call that explains the whole variance. Listen to it.
One late credit note moved forty thousand dollars across two months.
Hand your manager the bridge, not the spreadsheet - one page, every line explained.
